task: Nail the unique partially-revealing (PR) equilibrium of the K=3 CRRA REE strict contour-Phi operator (G=11, 729 interior prices) at ~100-dec, via hybrid damped-Picard -> accurate-Jacobian Newton.

scalar_micro_benchmark_100dec.note: 20000 evals each of exp/atanh/log; gmpy2 precision=333 bits (~100 dec).
scalar_micro_benchmark_100dec.winner: flint.arb is 4x-20x FASTER than gmpy2.mpfr at 100-dec scalars; the Cython/flint path is the correct fast backend.

validation_gate.comment: Cython Phi at 100-dec reproduces python-flint phi_sigdelta_strict_fast at 200-dec to 2.4e-91 over the persist2 interior price surface (diff = the 100-dec precision floor, exactly as expected).

picard_warmup.comment: Picard rides the stable manifold down to ||Phi-P||inf=0.0664 in ~5 evals, then the damping omega collapses (0.3 -> 5.9e-4) and it CANNOT descend further -- this is the '0.06 floor' the task targets.

accurate_jacobian.method: column k = (Phi(P+eps e_k) - Phi(P))/eps with eps=arb('1e-25'), the subtraction done IN ARB at 100-dec then downcast to float64; -1 on the diagonal for the -P term. 729 columns parallel (fork, nproc=4).
accurate_jacobian.KEY_FINDING: The strict Phi operator is GENUINELY DISCONTINUOUS in P at contour-node ties: perturbing p_cell by ANY eps (1e-25..1e-4) produces a CONSTANT ~0.027 jump in Phi[self] (symmetric in +/-eps). So 151/729 diagonal 'derivatives' are spurious spikes up to 6.5e23, and cond(J)=5.6e25. This is NOT a float64-accuracy artifact (the prior nail's claimed flaw): the accurate arb Jacobian makes the spikes WORSE, not better, because they are real jumps / a tiny eps. Removing the 151 spike diagonals (-> -1) yields cond=1.4e4, matching the prior frozen-system's 1417: the spikes ARE the entire ill-conditioning.

newton_descent_test.interpretation: BOTH the raw accurate Jacobian AND the well-conditioned spike-regularized Jacobian (cond=1.4e4) bottom out at strict ||Phi-P||inf=0.06574 at alpha=0.01 -- INDISTINGUISHABLE from the Picard plateau 0.06640. Larger steps EXPLODE the residual (alpha=1 -> 2.2-2.3) because the contour-crossing topology (active set) flips in hundreds of cells once the step is finite; smaller steps are pinned at the floor. The Newton direction yields ZERO net descent inside the region where the active set is valid.

representation_sensitivity_clincher.note: The SAME plateau P, saved to 120-decimal strings and reloaded, jumps from ||Phi-P||inf=0.0664 to 0.1381 -- driven ENTIRELY by ONE cell, (8,3,5), whose residual flips from ~0.066 to 0.138 (the bulk inf-cell (3,8,9) stays at exactly 0.0663990). A sub-1e-100 perturbation of the price flips a contour-crossing (dp*dn)<=0 tie and jumps Phi by ~0.072 in that cell. This is the discontinuity made directly visible: Phi(P) is NOT a function continuous in P to better than O(1e-1) at tie cells, so NO root-finder (any precision) can pin a residual below the tie-jump scale there. d_FR (0.26945) is robust to the reload (it is an RMS over 729 cells).

HEADLINE.verdict: The accurate Jacobian does NOT break the 0.06 floor. The floor is NOT a Picard-instability artifact removable by root-finding -- it is set by the GENUINE NON-SMOOTHNESS (discontinuity) of the strict contour-Phi operator at node-tie crossings. The task's premise (that the prior nail failed only due to a float64 FD_eps=1e-7 Jacobian, and an accurate arb Jacobian at eps=1e-25 would descend the 13 unstable modes) is FALSIFIED on three independent grounds: (1) the accurate arb Jacobian at eps=1e-25 produces spurious 1e23 discontinuity spikes on 151/729 diagonals (cond 5.6e25) because Phi truly JUMPS ~0.027 under any eps perturbation of p_cell; (2) even after regularizing the 151 spikes away to a well-conditioned cond=1.4e4 system (matching the prior frozen-system's 1417), BOTH Newton directions are pinned at strict ||Phi-P||inf=0.0657 = the Picard floor, with larger steps exploding the residual via active-set flips; (3) the SAME plateau P reloaded from 120-digit strings jumps 0.0664->0.1381 from a single tie-cell, proving Phi is discontinuous to O(0.1) in P. This independently reproduces the prior flint_pr_nail run's conclusion. The lowest-residual reachable point (bulk floor 0.0664) is the Picard plateau, saved as P_star.npy.

d_FR_definition: RMS distance of interior P from P_FR = sigmoid(tau*(u1+u2+u3)), tau=2.
